cases.answer: Code under the main guard only runs when you execute the file directly, like python script.py. If another module imports it, that block is skipped, so you can import its functions without kicking off the command line logic.
The main guard stops the module from running any code at all when it is imported, so imports have no side effects, and it also makes the script run faster because Python compiles it differently.

cases.answer: A resource-oriented API is built around nouns like orders or customers, each with a stable URL, and you use the HTTP methods like GET, PUT and DELETE to change their state. RPC style is built around verbs, like createOrder or cancelOrder endpoints. A few action endpoints are fine for real commands like cancel, but most of the API should be modeled as resources.
A descriptor is just Python's word for a docstring, the text that describes what a function does. You see them in the output of help().

cases.answer: dns-prefetch only resolves the domain early, and preconnect goes further and opens the TCP and TLS connection. preload fetches something the current page needs soon, and prefetch is low priority for a future page. modulepreload is the same as preload but it also executes the module immediately.
evidence: opens the TCP and TLS connection
cases.notes: Four hints are right; modulepreload does not execute the module. A false secondary claim caps the answer at PARTIAL.

cases.answer: If teams release on their own schedules and the shared parts are stable, I'd publish a versioned package with semantic versioning, changelogs and a deprecation policy, so each team upgrades when it is ready. If the teams are tightly coupled and change things together, a monorepo makes atomic changes easier, but it needs clear ownership and CI that only runs the affected suites.
